section: Andhra region under the Company - Machilipatnam, Ceded Districts, early administration and revenue
subsections: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat
Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts
Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

accepted.s: The Circuit Committee, while examining revenue administration in the Andhra region, recommended which of the following?
o: Replacement of ryotwari by permanent settlement
Abolition of the auction system of revenue collection
Continuation of the auction system with higher minimum bids
Transfer of revenue collection entirely to village panchayats
accepted.x: The Circuit Committee recommended against the highest-bidder auction system because it harmed both the government and the ryots. Munro subsequently abolished auctions in Rayalaseema.
accepted.tq: Identify the recommendation by linking the committee with the administrative problem it addressed.
accepted.sec: Circuit Committee - purpose, findings

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched with the judicial hierarchy in the Madras Presidency?
accepted.x: The Munsiff Court functioned at the taluk level, while the Zilla Court functioned at the district level. Sadar Adalats were apex courts for natives at Madras.
accepted.tq: Use the administrative level as the anchor for matching the court.
accepted.sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

accepted.s: The Zilla or District Court functioned under a District Judge. The post of District Judge was created by the:
accepted.x: The post of District Judge was created under the Cornwallis Code of 1793. The Madras Regulations of 1816 related chiefly to Munsiff and Panchayat courts.
accepted.tq: Use the legislation–office association and reject neighbouring judicial enactments.
accepted.sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

accepted.s:
With reference to the judicial system in the Madras Presidency, consider the following statements:
1. The powers of the Provincial Courts of Appeal or Circuit Courts were expanded in 1820.
2. The Sadar Adalat dealt with civil cases and the Sadar Faujdari Adalat dealt with criminal cases.
3. Both Sadar courts functioned at Madras as apex courts for natives.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Provincial appellate powers were expanded in 1820, while the Sadar Adalat and Sadar Faujdari Adalat were the civil and criminal apex courts for natives at Madras.
accepted.tq: Check each court by its level, jurisdiction and location before selecting the code.
accepted.sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

accepted.s: The Madras Supreme Court established in 1801 primarily exercised jurisdiction over:
o: All village panchayats in the Ceded Districts
Revenue disputes only in the Northern Circars
Native subjects throughout the Madras Presidency
accepted.x: The Madras Supreme Court, established in 1801, dealt with British subjects in Madras town. It was distinct from the Sadar courts for natives.
accepted.tq: Distinguish courts by their subject jurisdiction and territorial coverage.
accepted.sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the effect of the Indian High Courts Act, 1861, in the Madras Presidency?
o: It replaced the Sadar courts with the Madras High Court in 1862.
It transferred all civil powers from District Judges to Collectors.
It created the first Munsiff courts in every large village.
It established the Madras Supreme Court and abolished the Sadar courts.
accepted.x: Under the Indian High Courts Act, 1861, the Madras High Court was established in 1862 and replaced the Sadar courts.
accepted.tq: Separate the year of the Act from the year in which the court came into existence.
accepted.sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. CPC — 1859
2. IPC — 1860
3. CrPC — 1861
accepted.x: The Civil Procedure Code was associated with 1859, the Indian Penal Code with 1860 and the Criminal Procedure Code with 1861.
accepted.tq: Test the coded year associations individually rather than relying on the sequence alone.
accepted.sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

accepted.s: The introduction of British judicial procedure in place of village panchayats was criticised mainly because it:
o: was slow and costly and contributed to litigation and debt
made justice quicker and less expensive
reduced litigation and eliminated rural debt
transferred all judicial powers to hereditary village officers
accepted.x: British judicial procedure displaced village panchayats and was criticised as slow and costly. It increased litigation and contributed to indebtedness.
accepted.tq: Select the option that combines all the stated consequences without reversing the criticism.
accepted.sec: Judicial courts hierarchy - Munsiff, Zilla, Sadr Adalat

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Thomas Munro:
1. He was the President of the Judicial Commission in 1814.
2. The report of the Judicial Commission was submitted in April 1816.
3. Most of the recommendations in the report were accepted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Munro presided over the Judicial Commission in 1814, whose report was submitted in April 1816 and was largely accepted.
accepted.tq: Combine office, date and outcome in a single administrative sequence.
accepted.sec: Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts

accepted.s: The Madras Regulations of 1816 provided for:
o: Abolition of all village-level judicial institutions
Munsiff and Panchayat courts as courts of first instance
Transfer of civil justice from District Judges to Collectors
Creation of the Madras High Court
accepted.x: The Madras Regulations of 1816 established Munsiff courts and Panchayat courts in every large village and district as courts of first instance.
accepted.tq: Match the regulation with its immediate institutional reform.
accepted.sec: Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts

accepted.s: Under the judicial arrangements associated with Munro's reforms, village officials were permitted to deal with:
accepted.x: Village officials handled petty thefts under the reformed arrangements. Serious judicial and appellate matters remained with higher courts.
accepted.tq: Distinguish limited local jurisdiction from the powers of higher courts.
accepted.sec: Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the separation of judicial and revenue functions in 1816 is correct?
o: Collectors received all criminal and civil powers in the same year.
Munsiffs were abolished and replaced by District Collectors.
Collectors lost their judicial powers, while civil justice remained with District Judges.
District Judges lost civil powers, which were transferred entirely to Collectors.
accepted.x: Collectors lost their judicial powers in 1816, and civil justice remained with District Judges. Under the ryotwari arrangement, some magisterial powers later returned to Collectors.
accepted.tq: Watch for the reversed authority trap involving Collectors and District Judges.
accepted.sec: Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts

accepted.s: In which year did Magistrates receive powers to punish under the judicial reforms described for the Madras Presidency?
accepted.x: Magistrates received powers to punish in 1818. The year 1816 is associated with the separation of Collectors' judicial powers and the establishment of Munsiff and Panchayat courts.
accepted.tq: Separate closely connected reform dates before choosing the year.
accepted.sec: Munro's judicial reforms - Indian officials, village courts

accepted.s: Who created thanas under the supervision of darogas in the early British police administration?
accepted.x: Cornwallis created thanas under darogas, who were Indian officers assisted by constables. Darogas were criticised for abusing their power.
accepted.tq: Use the founder–institution association and avoid swapping judicial and police reformers.
accepted.sec: Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the daroga system:
1. A daroga was an Indian police officer.
2. Darogas were assisted by constables.
3. Darogas were widely known for abusing their power.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The daroga system placed Indian officers in charge of thanas with constables assisting them, but abuse of authority was a recognised criticism.
accepted.tq: Verify composition, subordinate personnel and criticism separately.
accepted.sec: Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

accepted.s: In the Madras Presidency, the traditional village watchmen were:
o: placed directly under the Sadar Adalat
abolished and replaced by military courts
supplemented by a central police force under a District Superintendent
accepted.x: Traditional village watchmen continued but were supplemented by a central police force under a District Superintendent. The force was feared because of corruption.
accepted.tq: Distinguish supplementation from abolition or replacement.
accepted.sec: Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

accepted.s: Munro's police reforms of 1816 transferred police supervision from:
o: Darogas to the Board of Revenue
accepted.x: Munro's changes in 1816 transferred police supervision from judges to Collectors. This was part of the reorganisation of administrative powers.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of transfer by identifying both the former and new authority.
accepted.sec: Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

accepted.s: The Madras District Police Act was enacted in:
accepted.x: The Madras District Police Act was enacted in 1859. The other years relate to judicial or police-administrative changes mentioned in the same context.
accepted.tq: Use the year-specific legislation trap and distinguish it from the judicial enactments.
accepted.sec: Police administration - Daroga system, village watch

accepted.s: The Madras Board of Revenue was established in:
accepted.x: The Madras Board of Revenue was set up in 1786 and became the state-level apex of the revenue hierarchy.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Board's establishment year from the years of territorial acquisition and judicial reform.
accepted.sec: Board of Revenue - establishment, functions

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Revenue level)
A. State
B. District
C. Taluk
D. Village

List-II (Officer)
1. Tahsildar
2. Collector
3. Board of Revenue
4. Karanam and Munsab

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: The Board of Revenue was at the state level, the Collector at the district level, the Tahsildar at the taluk level and the Karanam and Munsab at the village level.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure state and village pairs, then complete the intermediate levels.
accepted.sec: Board of Revenue - establishment, functions

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the revenue hierarchy between the taluk and village levels?
o: Sub-Collector at taluk level; Board of Revenue at village level
Munsab at taluk level; Tahsildar at village level
Tahsildar at taluk level; Karanam and Munsab at village level
Collector at taluk level; Deputy Tahsildar at village level
accepted.x: The Tahsildar was the taluk-level officer, while the hereditary village officers were the Karanam and Munsab.
accepted.tq: Compare adjacent administrative levels to detect the reversed hierarchy.
accepted.sec: Board of Revenue - establishment, functions

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with the revenue hierarchy?

1. Division — Sub-Collector or Revenue Officer
2. Firka — Deputy Tahsildar or Firka Revenue Inspector
3. District — Collector
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. The hierarchy placed the Collector at the district level, Sub-Collector or Revenue Officer at the divisional level and Deputy Tahsildar or Firka Revenue Inspector at the firka level.
accepted.tq: Check each officer against the precise administrative tier.
accepted.sec: Board of Revenue - establishment, functions

accepted.s: The Andhra Board of Revenue was formed in 1953 primarily to:
o: link the government with the districts after the creation of Andhra State
transfer the Ceded Districts to the Nizam
abolish the office of the District Collector
accepted.x: The Andhra Board of Revenue was formed in 1953 after Andhra State was created. It served as a link between the government and the districts.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution's purpose from the administrative transition that produced it.
accepted.sec: Board of Revenue - establishment, functions

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding sericulture in Rayalaseema:
1. British promotion of the crop in the Ceded Districts dates to the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
2. Dharmavaram and Madanapalle are present-day silk hubs.
3. The crop was introduced into Rayalaseema only after the formation of Andhra State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The historical association is with British promotion in the Ceded Districts during the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, not only after Andhra State was formed.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute time claim and retain the two historically precise statements.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s:
Which of the following is the correct chronological order in which major territorial components of present-day Andhra took shape under Company rule?

A. Ceded Districts
B. Circars
C. Nellore-Chittoor
D. Guntur
accepted.x: The Circars came under Company control in 1766, Guntur in 1788, the Ceded Districts in 1800 and Nellore-Chittoor in 1801.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest territorial changes first, then place the middle events by year.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the territorial contrast under British and Nizam rule?
o: The coast and Rayalaseema passed to the Company, while Telangana remained under the Nizam.
Telangana passed to the Company, while the coast remained with the Nizam.
Rayalaseema remained under the Nizam, while Telangana passed to the Company.
The entire Andhra region remained under the Nizam until 1953.
accepted.x: The coast and Rayalaseema came under Company rule, whereas Telangana remained under the Nizam. This produced an important political and administrative contrast within the Telugu-speaking regions.
accepted.tq: Use the paired regional contrast and beware of reversing the two territories.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The growing divergence between the fertile and educated Circars and the arid and neglected Ceded Districts later influenced debates surrounding the:
accepted.x: The contrasting development of the Circars and the Ceded Districts later shaped the Sri Bagh Pact debate. The other pacts belong to different political contexts.
accepted.tq: Link a regional socio-economic contrast with the agreement it later influenced.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Thomas Munro in the Andhra region is correct?
o: He introduced mahalwari settlement from Punjab into the Ceded Districts and died at Hyderabad in 1827.
He introduced permanent settlement from Bengal into the Circars and died at Madras in 1801.
He introduced zamindari in Rayalaseema and died at Nellore in 1816.
He introduced ryotwari from the Bara Mahals into the Ceded Districts and died at Pattikonda as Governor in 1827.
accepted.x: Munro brought the ryotwari system from the Bara Mahals to the Ceded Districts. He died at Pattikonda in Kurnool district in 1827 while serving as Governor.
accepted.tq: Combine the reformer's policy, source region, destination and death details without swapping settlement systems.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ceded Districts — arid and neglected region
Most Collectors — independent functioning without native subordinates or interpreters
accepted.x: Most Collectors depended on interpreters or corrupt native subordinates because they did not know Telugu. Munro and Brown were exceptions; Munro himself was a Telugu-speaking Collector.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses the general rule and its stated exceptions.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The concentration of revenue, magisterial and police powers in the office of the District Collector made the Collector the:
o: pivot of British rule and an agent of the end of village autonomy
hereditary head of the Board of Revenue
chief appellate judge of the Madras Supreme Court
accepted.x: By combining revenue, magisterial and police powers, the District Collector became the pivot of British administration. This concentration of authority weakened village autonomy.
accepted.tq: Infer institutional importance from the combination of powers held by one office.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: A plea before the Supreme Court sought a separate revenue judicial service cadre on the ground that revenue officers without legal training should not decide land-title disputes. The plea invoked which constitutional provision?
accepted.x: The plea invoked Article 14 and argued that officers without legal training should not adjudicate land-title disputes. The Supreme Court issued notice on the plea.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional article directly linked to the stated legal argument.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Who was identified as the Chief Justice of India when the Supreme Court issued notice on the plea for a separate revenue judicial service cadre?
accepted.x: The notice was issued by the Supreme Court under Chief Justice Surya Kant. The plea concerned the adjudication of land-title disputes by revenue officers.
accepted.tq: Test the current-affairs office-holder directly rather than confusing it with earlier office-holders.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
